779:             "the maximum allowable time of max_time = {} (did you"
780:             " supply event times in "
781:             "seconds?)".format(events.max(), max_time)
782:         )
783:     # Make sure event locations are 1-d np ndarrays
784:     if events.ndim != 1:
785:         raise ValueError(
786:             "Event times should be 1-d numpy ndarray, "
787:             "but shape={}".format(events.shape)
788:         )
789:     # Make sure event times are increasing
790:     if (np.diff(events) < 0).any():
791:         raise ValueError("Events should be in increasing order.")
792: 
793: 
794: def validate_frequencies(frequencies, max_freq, min_freq, allow_negatives=False):
795:     """Check that a 1-d frequency ndarray is well-formed, and raises
796:     errors if not.
797: 
798:     Parameters
799:     ----------
800:     frequencies : np.ndarray, shape=(n,)
801:         Array of frequency values
802:     max_freq : float
803:         If a frequency is found above this pitch, a ValueError will be raised.
804:         (Default value = 5000.)
805:     min_freq : float
806:         If a frequency is found below this pitch, a ValueError will be raised.
807:         (Default value = 20.)
808:     allow_negatives : bool
809:         Whether or not to allow negative frequency values.
810:     """
811:     # If flag is true, map frequencies to their absolute value.
812:     if allow_negatives:
813:         frequencies = np.abs(frequencies)
814:     # Make sure no frequency values are huge
815:     if (np.abs(frequencies) > max_freq).any():
816:         raise ValueError(
817:             "A frequency of {} was found which is greater than "
818:             "the maximum allowable value of max_freq = {} (did "
819:             "you supply frequency values in "
820:             "Hz?)".format(frequencies.max(), max_freq)
821:         )
822:     # Make sure no frequency values are tiny
823:     if (np.abs(frequencies) < min_freq).any():
824:         raise ValueError(
825:             "A frequency of {} was found which is less than the "
826:             "minimum allowable value of min_freq = {} (did you "
827:             "supply frequency values in "
828:             "Hz?)".format(frequencies.min(), min_freq)
829:         )
830:     # Make sure frequency values are 1-d np ndarrays
831:     if frequencies.ndim != 1:
832:         raise ValueError(
833:             "Frequencies should be 1-d numpy ndarray, "
834:             "but shape={}".format(frequencies.shape)
835:         )
836: 
837: 
838: def has_kwargs(function):
839:     r"""Determine whether a function has ``**kwargs``.
840: 
841:     Parameters
842:     ----------
843:     function : callable
844:         The function to test
845: 
846:     Returns
847:     -------
848:     True if function accepts arbitrary keyword arguments.
849:     False otherwise.
850:     """
851:     sig = inspect.signature(function)
852: 
853:     for param in list(sig.parameters.values()):
854:         if param.kind == param.VAR_KEYWORD:
855:             return True
856: 
857:     return False
858: 
859: 
860: def filter_kwargs(_function, *args, **kwargs):
861:     r"""Given a function and args and keyword args to pass to it, call the function
862:     but using only the keyword arguments which it accepts.  This is equivalent
863:     to redefining the function with an additional ``**kwargs`` to accept slop
864:     keyword args.
865: 
866:     If the target function already accepts ``**kwargs`` parameters, no filtering
867:     is performed.
868: 
869:     Parameters
870:     ----------
871:     _function : callable
872:         Function to call.  Can take in any number of args or kwargs
873:     *args
874:     **kwargs
875:         Arguments and keyword arguments to _function.
876:     """
877:     if has_kwargs(_function):
878:         return _function(*args, **kwargs)
879: 
880:     # Get the list of function arguments
881:     func_code = _function.__code__
882:     function_args = func_code.co_varnames[: func_code.co_argcount]
883:     # Construct a dict of those kwargs which appear in the function
884:     filtered_kwargs = {}
885:     for kwarg, value in list(kwargs.items()):
886:         if kwarg in function_args:
887:             filtered_kwargs[kwarg] = value
888:     # Call the function with the supplied args and the filtered kwarg dict
889:     return _function(*args, **filtered_kwargs)
890: 
891: 
892: def intervals_to_durations(intervals):
893:     """Convert an array of n intervals to their n durations.
894: 
895:     Parameters
896:     ----------
897:     intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(n, 2)
898:         An array of time intervals, as returned by
899:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_intervals()`.
900:         The ``i`` th interval spans time ``intervals[i, 0]`` to
901:         ``intervals[i, 1]``.
902: 
903:     Returns
904:     -------
905:     durations : np.ndarray, shape=(n,)
906:         Array of the duration of each interval.
907: 
908:     """
909:     validate_intervals(intervals)
910:     return np.abs(np.diff(intervals, axis=-1)).flatten()
911: 
912: 
913: def hz_to_midi(freqs):
914:     """Convert Hz to MIDI numbers
915: 
916:     Parameters
917:     ----------
918:     freqs : number or ndarray
919:         Frequency/frequencies in Hz
920: 
921:     Returns
922:     -------
923:     midi : number or ndarray
924:         MIDI note numbers corresponding to input frequencies.
925:         Note that these may be fractional.
926:     """
927:     return 12.0 * (np.log2(freqs) - np.log2(440.0)) + 69.0
928: 
929: 
930: def midi_to_hz(midi):
931:     """Convert MIDI numbers to Hz
932: 
933:     Parameters
934:     ----------
